claims.claim: For p not dividing the base b, collision detection is exactly repeated-state detection on mismatch-only normalized prefix sums. Moreover, every collision has a witness containing at most p mismatching aligned positions, although its length may exceed p.
claims.evidence: For r<e, direct expansion gives b^e(A_d(e)-A_d(r))=F(r,e-r)-F(r+d,e-r) modulo p. Since p does not divide b, b^e is invertible, proving fingerprint equality iff A_d(r)=A_d(e). Requiring an actual mismatch excludes equal-content pairs. A_d changes only immediately after mismatch positions, so repeats among B_0,...,B_m are exactly genuine collisions at displacement d. If a collision contains more than p mismatches, consider its state before the first mismatch and after each of its first p mismatches. Two of these p+1 elements of F_p coincide, yielding a contained colliding subinterval with between 1 and p mismatches. Exact exhaustive checks found no exception across 27,484 invertible instances and 79,742 colliding aligned intervals, including 6,622 intervals with more than p mismatches.
claims.search_method: Independent field-algebra proof, boundary and quantifier analysis, followed by exhaustive exact-integer enumeration over bases 2 through 5, several lengths, and primes 2,3,5,7,11 whenever p did not divide b.

claims.claim: In the word-RAM model with p=n^{O(1)}, there is an exact deterministic algorithm running in O(n log n+n+min{D,M,n min(n,p)}) time, where D is the number of distinct substring contents and M is the number of unequal unordered character-position pairs. Consequently the requested O(n log n) bound holds when p=O(log n), D=O(n log n), or M=O(n log n).
claims.evidence: For invertible b, LCE jumps use O(1+m_d) work at displacement d, or stop after p mismatches, so the record/work count is O(n+sum_d min(m_d,p)). Each unequal unordered position pair occurs at exactly one displacement, giving sum_d m_d=M, while m_d<=n-d gives sum_d min(m_d,p)=O(min(M,n min(n,p))). Complete (d,state) keys occupy O(1) words because p=n^{O(1)} and can be radix-sorted with O(n) bucket overhead after deterministic O(n log n) suffix/LCE preprocessing. Independently, character-boundary loci of a compact suffix tree correspond bijectively to distinct substring contents; the sum of trimmed edge lengths is D. Traversing them produces one (length,fingerprint) record per content in O(D), and duplicate keys are exactly unequal-content collisions. D and M can be computed during preprocessing, permitting selection of the cheaper route. When p divides b, the verified algorithm in claim 2 is already O(n log n), hence also satisfies this upper bound. Substituting any of p=O(log n), D=O(n log n), or M=O(n log n) gives O(n log n).
claims.search_method: Independent operation-count proof for the mismatch and suffix-tree routes, combinatorial verification of sum_d m_d=M, word-size/radix-sort analysis, and exhaustive comparison of both detectors against brute force on the checker’s finite instances.

claims.claim: The target has a complete O(n log n) exact solution in the noninvertible case p divides b.
claims.evidence: If p divides b, every positive power of b vanishes modulo p, so every nonempty most-significant-first fingerprint is exactly its last character modulo p. For endpoints e<f in one residue class, all allowable equal-length suffixes agree exactly when R_e=s[e]...s[0] is a prefix of R_f. If the prefix test fails after t matching reversed characters, the length-(t+1) suffixes are unequal but have identical fingerprints. If all consecutive endpoint pairs in a residue class satisfy the prefix relation, transitivity makes every pair satisfy it; conversely, any failed consecutive test supplies a collision. LCP support on the reversed string plus deterministic residue grouping takes O(n log n), and all comparisons are exact. Exhaustive testing of 9,723 p-divides-b instances agreed with brute force.
claims.search_method: Independent modular-degeneration proof, endpoint-prefix equivalence and transitivity audit, followed by exhaustive exact-integer testing for bases 2 through 6 and all tested prime divisors.

claims.claim: Collisions cannot occur at length L when b^L<=p, but checking only power-of-two lengths, only lexicographically adjacent contents, or relying on monotonicity in the length is insufficient.
claims.evidence: Two distinct canonical length-L base-b words have distinct integer values whose nonzero difference has absolute value at most b^L-1. When b^L<=p, that difference is strictly smaller than p and cannot vanish modulo p. For b=2, p=5, and S=000101, exact evaluation gives fingerprint arrays [0,0,0,1,0,1], [0,0,1,2,1], [0,1,2,0], [1,2,0], [2,0], and [0] for lengths 1 through 6. The only unequal-content collision length is 3, between 000 and 101. Hence lengths 1,2,4 are collision-free, collision existence is nonmonotone, and the colliding length-3 contents are nonadjacent in the lexicographic list 000,001,010,101.
claims.witness: b=2, p=5, S=000101; the unequal contents 000 and 101 collide at length 3 with fingerprint 0, while every power-of-two length present in S is collision-free and their positions in the lexicographically sorted distinct-content list are nonadjacent.
claims.search_method: Direct integer-range proof plus exact reproduction of every fingerprint and every unequal-content collision in the stated finite witness; the threshold was also exhaustively checked on all finite instances covered by the checker.

target_evidence: The exact source target asks for an O(n log n) or linear detector for an arbitrary supplied prime, with a small false-rejection probability merely permitted. The draft proves exact O(n log n) algorithms for p dividing b and for the invertible regimes p=O(log n), D=O(n log n), or M=O(n log n), together with valid structural reductions and counterexamples to tempting shortcuts. It does not bound its runtime by O(n log n) when p does not divide b, p is superlogarithmic, and both D and M are superlinear; its displayed adaptive bound may then be quadratic. The final writeup explicitly identifies that remaining regime and labels the resolution PARTIAL, so the surviving results are material but incomplete and the claimed resolution is accurate.
